purpose: Find whether the free GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 Chromium 151 can run actual WebGL2 via Mesa llvmpipe with explicit LP_NUM_THREADS=2, without fallback to SwiftShader; no scored performance or gate threshold change.
trigger: one initial pull_request.opened event, attempt 1; no retry, favorable-run replacement or environment selection after data

scenarios.source: Noon browserArgs('webgl') with original SwiftShader flags
Chrome ANGLE GL backend --use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl; LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=true; GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe; LP_NUM_THREADS=2
Chrome ANGLE GL/EGL backend --use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl; LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=true; GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe; LP_NUM_THREADS=2; EGL_PLATFORM=surfaceless

acceptanceOfPilot: Mesa candidate is feasible only if observed unmasked renderer identifies llvmpipe and all actual WebGL2 draw/readback proofs pass; a fallback to SwiftShader, unavailable identity, invalid readback or mismatched browser is not feasible.
next: If a Mesa configuration passes: separate preregistered identical-package A/A precision study with original workloads and scorer. This pilot is never PR #1875 candidate acceptance.
